questions.question: Nayib Bukele registered his candidacy to seek a third six-year term as president of which country?
questions.explanation: Bukele submitted his application to the Supreme Electoral Court to contest El Salvador's presidential election in 2027.
questions.context: 2027 Salvadoran presidential election: Incumbent president of El Salvador Nayib Bukele presents his presidential candidacy to the Supreme Electoral Court seeking registration ahead of the 2027 elections. He is running for a third presidential term that will last six years.

questions.question: The International Court of Justice determined that which country committed genocide against the Rohingya people?
questions.explanation: Judges at the UN's top court, the International Court of Justice, issued a ruling stating that Myanmar was guilty of genocide against the Rohingya.
questions.context: Rohingya genocide case: The International Court of Justice rules that Myanmar has committed genocide against the Rohingya people.

questions.question: Which Latin American country signed a free trade agreement with the Philippines at the APEC summit, marking the Philippines' first such deal with the region?
questions.explanation: During the APEC meeting held in Shenzhen, the Philippines signed its inaugural free trade deal with a Latin American nation by partnering with Chile.
questions.context: APEC China 2026 > Chile–Philippines relations: The Philippines and Chile sign a free trade agreement as part of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China, marking the former's first such agreement with a Latin American country.

questions.question: Over 300 garment factories were forced to shut down due to widespread minimum wage demonstrations in which country?
questions.explanation: Ongoing wage disputes led to the closure of 341 apparel manufacturing sites across Bangladesh as police clashed with protesters.
questions.context: 2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests: Across Bangladesh, 341 garment factories remain closed amid ongoing minimum wage protests, as police fire tear gas and stun grenades to disperse demonstrators in Ashulia and clear blockades on the Dhaka–Mymensingh Highway in Gazipur, while Bangladesh Nationalist Party members take up positions along highway areas in Sreepur and authorities tighten security at Kashimpur Central Jail.

questions.question: Sandagiin Byambatsogt stepped in as acting president following the resignation of Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh in which country?
questions.explanation: Mongolia's parliament accepted President Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh's resignation, leaving legislative chairman Byambatsogt to lead until elections are held.
questions.context: Corruption in Mongolia: The State Great Khural accepts the resignation of Mongolian president Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh. The chamber's chairman, Sandagiin Byambatsogt, assumes the acting presidency until a new election is held within four months.
